subject: Re: Coordinating breach communications, legal hold & subprocessor access windows
messages:
From: James Smith <j.smith@finex.com>
To: lukas.meyer@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@finex.com
Date: Fri, 9 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Potential exposed objects observed — request for evidence preservation and access windows

Lukas,

Apologies for the early message. Our security team (FinexCorp) identified a pattern of anomalous GET requests against a small set of S3 objects that appear to be customer records with PII. At this point we are treating this as a potential data exposure and need Redwood's cooperation to preserve and transfer forensic evidence.

Specifically we need: (1) a 72-hour preservation hold on the implicated object keys and related logs, (2) an export of access logs and object metadata for the keys listed below within 48–72 hours, and (3) confirmation of which subprocessors or downstream systems (including any marketplace or analytics partners) could have seen the same objects.

Sample object keys (partial):
- s3://redwood-prod/customer-data/finex/obj-7a3f2d.json
- s3://redwood-prod/customer-data/finex/session-archive-20270430.tar.gz

We have a legal request on standby; our counsel will send the signed evidence transfer if you confirm the export/transfer process. Please let us know the expected ETA for the preservation snapshot and the secure transfer mechanism (SFTP, encrypted upload, or managed MFT).

Thanks — we want to move fast and avoid any additional exposure.

James Smith
Head of Security, FinexCorp
security@finex.com

---
(attachment: incident_sample_list.csv)

From: lukas.meyer@redwood.ai <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: James Smith <j.smith@finex.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 May 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential exposed objects observed — request for evidence preservation and access windows

James — thanks for the heads-up and for the sample keys. We are treating this as an active investigation and have kicked off our incident runbook. High level plan and immediate commitments: 

1) Preservation: We will place a 7-day preservation hold (immutable snapshot) on the buckets/objects you listed within the next 4 hours.
2) Initial evidence: Ops will produce a first-cut export (metadata + access logs hash + snapshot manifest) within 24 hours. Full evidence export (including object-level logs and forensic packet-level traces where available) targeted within 72 hours.
3) Subprocessors: Ops will provide the currently known list of subprocessors/systems with potential access (storage gateways, log-collector clusters, analytics pipelines) within 48 hours.
4) Transfer: We prefer a managed SFTP endpoint with client certs or our secure MFT (we will provide a pre-shared transfer URL). We will not share raw customer data until we receive a formal written request (signed by your legal contact).

Ben Carter (cc'd) will own the technical export. Kimberly Park (cc'd) will coordinate legal/data transfer requirements. Marissa Cole will coordinate communications.

Action items for you: please send the signed evidence request when ready and confirm whether you need object content or just metadata + logs + hashes. Also confirm whether Finex requires EU export documentation (SCCs) for any EU-subject records.

I'll follow up in a short thread with the runbook steps and the expected artifact names we will deliver.

— Lukas
Lukas Meyer
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: James Smith <j.smith@finex.com>, lukas.meyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 May 2027 10:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential exposed objects observed — request for evidence preservation and access windows

James / team — a few legal guardrails so we can move promptly without stepping over contractual obligations: 

- Evidence transfer: Redwood can provide access logs, object metadata, and cryptographic hashes of object content upon receipt of a formal, signed evidence request from Finex legal. If Finex requests actual object content, we require either (a) an executed DPA amendment allowing disclosure for forensic purposes or (b) a lawful request from a court/government.
- Subprocessor disclosures: We will provide a list of subprocessors and an attestation about whether those subprocessors had access to the implicated buckets/objects. We are unable to share the subprocessors' internal logs without their consent, but we will request and coordinate their evidence exports.
- Cross-border: If the export includes EEA-subject personal data, transfers outside the EEA will need appropriate safeguards (SCCs or adequacy mechanism). Please indicate whether the sample object keys contain EU residence data.
- Chain-of-custody: For any transfers of object content, we require the evidence transfer to use our managed MFT with end-to-end encryption and an MD5/SHA256 manifest for verification. We will keep an internal chain-of-custody log and provide a signed manifest.

Please have Finex legal send the signed request to legal@redwood.ai and copy the security mailbox so we can accept and approve the transfer. Once the request is received, Ben will execute the export and we will surface the secure link.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
(attachment: DPA-excerpt.pdf)

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: lukas.meyer@redwood.ai, James Smith <j.smith@finex.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 10 May 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential exposed objects observed — request for evidence preservation and access windows

Folks — operational update and artifact names for tracking. I've started the snapshot job and pulled preliminary logs. Itemized ETA and files: 

- Preservation snapshot: snapshot-redwood-prod-20270509-1100 (completed at 2027-05-09T11:00:00-07:00)
- Initial export (metadata + access log hashes): evidence_export_manifest.json (expected in 24 hours, i.e., by 2027-05-10T11:00:00-07:00)
- Full export (objects, additional logs): forensic_manifest.csv (expected within 72 hours, i.e., by 2027-05-12T11:00:00-07:00)

Subprocessors and systems that may have had access (high-level):
- storage-gateway-prod (internal S3 gateway)
- log-collector-eu / log-collector-us (aggregates application access logs)
- analytics-streams (redacted; third-party analytics partner "DataWave")

Notes and constraints: object content will be encrypted at rest; we will provide decrypted copies for transfer only after legal sign-off. The analytics partner is a downstream subprocessor with a separate DPA; we will request their assistance but cannot unilaterally retrieve their logs — coordination will take additional time.

Transfer options we support:
- Managed MFT (preferred) — URL will be provided after legal acceptance
- SFTP with client certificate (only for metadata and logs; object content transfers via MFT)

I've attached the two preliminary manifests for your intake. If Finex provides the signed request today, we'll aim to complete the initial export within the 24-hour window.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Cloud Operations, Redwood Inference
(attachments: evidence_export_manifest.json, forensic_manifest.csv)
